verified_title: GigaWorld-Policy: An Efficient Action-Centered World–Action Model
problem: Joint world/action diffusion spends inference time generating long future-video sequences even when only action chunks are needed. Unrestricted cross-modal attention can make action prediction depend on future tokens that are unavailable when the video branch is omitted.
contribution: A5B Wan2.2 world/action policy uses action-centered causal masking and large-scale embodied-video pretraining. Future-video prediction acts as training supervision but is optional at inference, allowing an action-only path and reusable context KV cache.
algorithm: Current multiview observations and proprioception attend within their block; actions may attend to present observations/state but not future-video tokens; future video additionally attends to actions. Language enters through cross-attention. Train video-only on embodied data, then joint flow matching with action/video loss weights5/1. Predict48 action steps and sparse future images every12 steps; sample actions alone by default.
observations: Language, proprioception and three RGB views (left/front/right) composed into one image and encoded by a shared VAE. Visual tokens use2D positions and state/action tokens1D temporal positions. Camera composition and viewpoint availability are part of the learned representation.
actions: Continuous embodiment-specific48-step chunks. Real experiments use6DoF AgileX PiPER gripper arms; exact joint/Cartesian action dimensionality and physical control frequency NOT_EXTRACTED, so48steps cannot be converted into a claimed timing/deadline for Explorer.
embodiment_and_data: Approximately10000h of public human/robot video (dataset table totals are estimates), including EgoDex/Ego4D/Agibot/OXE/DROID/RoboMind and others, followed by target task action supervision. RoboTwin2.0 trains on2500 clean plus25000 randomized demonstrations across50 tasks. Real data-efficiency figure varies5/25/50 demonstrations/task. Supplementp13 reports6000GPUh/batch256 for pretraining, but GPU model is NOT_EXTRACTED.
experiments: RoboTwin50 tasks under clean/randomized scenes,100 test episodes/task, with clutter, lighting and table variations. Physical PiPER evaluation covers desk cleanup, QR scanning, sweeping and bowl stacking,20trials/task/method; each trial permits up to FIVE attempts. Real evaluation grants0.5 for grasp and0.5 for placement rather than uniformly binary task success. Additional ablations vary pretraining sources, future-frame stride and attention masking.
baselines: pi0.5, GigaBrain-0, X-VLA, Motus and Cosmos-Policy. Simulation/physical baseline subsets differ. Causal-mask versus unrestricted self-attention has similar physical score; its principal structural advantage is permitting action-only inference without future-token leakage.

limitations: Physical trials permit repeated attempts and partial scores; paper headings use success rate for both binary simulation and graded hardware evaluation. No confidence intervals or independent training-seed analysis were extracted. Several table/prose and main/appendix discrepancies affect exact effect sizes. The claimed sample efficiency concerns target-task demonstrations, not the10000h prerequisite. Future-frame PSNR/SSIM is visual reconstruction quality, not proof of grasp/contact dynamics. Fixed three-camera layouts,6DoF PiPER embodiment and A100 latency do not establish SO101/M3 or NX readiness.
code_and_license: A paper-level method description and public-source dataset citations were examined; no pinned repository, code, released checkpoints or licenses were audited or executed. License and release availability UNKNOWN rather than inferred from paper publication.
hardware_adaptation: ADAPT the causal factorization as an offline compact-policy experiment: train action prediction plus sparse future-observation supervision, then remove the future branch at inference. A5B backbone has substantial memory/runtime overhead beyond weights; benchmark any implementation on NX before a deployment claim. Retain existing Explorer controller settings, explicitly map actual state/action dimensions and camera order, and compare independent complete-task success against ACT.
